Trapping depends on width and texture: an 8-m strip reduced sediment loss by 97% and a 4.6-m strip retained 83%, efficiency rises sharply over the first 10 m and then tails off, 4 m grass buffers on 2 % slopes trapped almost 100 % of sandy loams but only 35 % of silty clay loams, and 30 m buffers did not prevent increased stream sedimentation after partial clearcutting in Oregon [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2]. Most quantified units are from high-income USA, Canada and the UK, outside the LIC/LMIC target; the Brazil, China and Mexico units are a cover-versus-suspended-solids correlation, an uncited assertion, farmer perceptions and a loss-framed statement [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11].

riparian_buffer__soil_erosion_risk__inco.mechanism: Riparian forest is reported to reduce sediment loading into streams, and properly designed buffers trap sediments from runoff passing through them [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_10, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1]. Farmers identified tree roots as preventing riverbank erosion during floods [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5].
riparian_buffer__soil_erosion_risk__inco.conditionality: The evidence is indirect: a correlation between riparian-zone forest cover and suspended solids in the Sarapuí River basin, Brazil, an uncited introductory assertion, farmer perceptions, and a loss-framed statement that replacing riparian forest increases bank erosion [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11]. It uses component proxies (sediment retention, streambank erosion) rather than field soil-erosion measures, and comes from upper-middle-income Brazil, China and Mexico, the scope of this row [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5].

riparian_buffer__water_quality_risk.mechanism: Properly designed buffers trap and remove sediments and nutrients from surface and subsurface runoff passing through them, and well-managed riparian vegetation filters most upland sediment and agricultural chemicals before they reach the stream [ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1]. Nitrate is reduced in subsurface water after passage through grass and forest strips [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_4], and shade from wooded buffers moderates diel fluctuations in stream temperature and limits warming after harvest [ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3].
riparian_buffer__water_quality_risk.conditionality: Effects depend on pollutant and design: wider strips did not reduce soluble herbicides but did reduce sediment-bound glyphosate, a meta-analysis found no effect of width on nitrogen removal while other cited work finds wider buffers more effective with diminishing returns, wooded buffers removed nitrate better but phosphates worse than grass, and nutrient-saturated buffers can become a source rather than a sink during high flow, ice thaw and bank erosion [ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_1, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_3, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_4, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_6]. The quantified reductions (sediment loss reduced by 97% by an 8-m strip; 80% to 90% nitrate reduction in subsurface water) come from high-income US studies, and the row includes sediment-retention and stream-temperature component proxies [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2, ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1]. Evidence spans the USA, Canada, the UK, Brazil, China and Mexico and is mostly cited secondary, adjacent to rather than inside the LIC/LMIC target [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_12, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_5, ev_nutrient_removal_meli19_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1].
